contents.name: §5.1, Definition 24: translation representation, joint PVM, spectrum condition and future-tube continuation
contents.support: The notes define the strongly continuous translation representation and joint PVM, impose support in the closed forward cone, and state strong continuity to the real boundary and holomorphy in the open future tube. The new definition makes these data explicit and adds no inference from moment reconstruction.

contents.name: §5.1, Definition 24 and Theorem 26 proof: bounded-insertion tube functions
contents.support: The source uses products of analytically continued translations and bounded local operators in its Reeh–Schlieder argument. The item supplies the complete spectral-integral norm, boundary-continuity, operator-norm derivative and finite-product argument locally.

contents.name: §5.1, Theorem 26 proof: edge-of-the-wedge is an additional analytic step
contents.support: The source invokes an edge-of-the-wedge theorem to pass from boundary vanishing to an analytic conclusion. It proves Reeh–Schlieder there, not a CPT or spin-statistics theorem; the interface records the additional hypotheses and theorem-specific duties.

sources.locator: §1.3, PDF pp. 8–9, equations (19)–(24); §2.1, Theorems 2.6 and 2.8, PDF pp. 15–19; complete 39-page PDF inspected. The author labels the notes incomplete.

contents.name: §1.3, equations (19)–(24): joint momentum PVM and forward-cone support
contents.support: The source identifies the joint momentum spectrum, its PVM representation of translations, and the closed forward cone. The interface uses the exact (+---) pairing convention and treats the joint PVM as additional input.

contents.name: §2.1, Theorem 2.8: Fourier support in the forward cone gives a tube boundary value
contents.support: The theorem states holomorphy and distributional boundary values in the backward tube for its Fourier-transform convention. Its printed proof refers to Streater–Wightman and Reed–Simon rather than supplying the proof; the local item proves the bounded-operator claim with its explicitly fixed opposite exponential convention.

contents.name: §2.1, Theorems 2.6 and 2.8: assumptions and analytic proof boundaries
contents.support: The notes distinguish reconstruction hypotheses, joint spectral support, and tube analyticity, and present the analytic route as an outline with external theorem references. The interface does not use them as a complete CPT or spin-statistics proof.

contents.name: §4.1–4.2: tube continuation, complexified symmetry, weak locality and scalar CPT proof
contents.support: The paper proves a restricted CPT result for real scalar fields in its noncommutative setting with O(1,1)×SO(2) symmetry and adapted locality. It supplies a scoped analytic comparison and explicitly does not supply the general four-dimensional finite-component theorem.

contents.name: §4.3: spin-statistics scope and locality requirements
contents.support: The paper notes that the standard spin-statistics argument depends on the field representation and microcausality, while its noncommutative setting has exceptions. The interface retains those scope limits and asserts no general theorem.
